html:
The Siona are a Tucanoan people of the Putumayo River on the border of Colombia and Ecuador. They number a few thousand.

They lived along the rivers by farming, fishing and hunting, and their shamans are known for yagé, the drink also called ayahuasca, used in healing and visions. Franciscan and Jesuit missions reached them in the 1600s, the rubber trade around 1900 brought disease and debt labour, and oil drilling and armed conflict have hit their land since the 1970s. Their close kin are the Secoya, and their neighbours include the Inga to the west.
sum: The Siona are a Tucanoan people of the Putumayo River on the border of Colombia and Ecuador. They number a few thousand.
